### blip-2-2301.12597v1

Requirement: `req_9a9be430e5ba45bff83d6a3ce1a4d2ed` · Status: `verified`

BLIP-2 uses a frozen pre-trained image encoder; it explores two state-of-the-art pre-trained vision transformer models: ViT-L/14 from CLIP and ViT-G/14 from EVA-CLIP.
The image encoder is frozen pre-trained, and BLIP-2 removes the last layer of the ViT, using the second-to-last layer's output features.

### flamingo-2204.14198v1

Requirement: `req_fc4e37577cfdbaec487b0362bdba1d67` · Status: `verified`

Flamingo's vision encoder is a pretrained Normalizer-Free ResNet (NFNet), specifically the F6 model.
The Flamingo vision encoder is pretrained with a contrastive objective (à la CLIP) on image-text pairs, using a two-term contrastive loss with mean-pooled image encoder output and mean-pooled BERT output; during main Flamingo training the vision encoder weights are frozen.
The vision encoder's role is to extract semantic spatial features (color, shape, nature, positions of objects); its final stage output is a 2D spatial grid of features X_f, to which a learnt temporal position encoding is added before flattening and concatenation, feeding the Perceiver Resampler.

## vision language bridge · Verified findings

### blip-2-2301.12597v1

Requirement: `req_9b812a56c386edc56b01ad7612222137` · Status: `verified`

BLIP-2 bridges the modality gap with a Querying Transformer (Q-Former), a lightweight module that is the trainable connector between a frozen image encoder and a frozen LLM; it is pre-trained in two stages.
The Q-Former uses 32 learnable queries of dimension 768; its output query representation Z (32x768) is a bottleneck much smaller than the frozen image features (e.g., 257x1024 for ViT-L/14), forcing the queries to extract visual information most relevant to the text.
The Q-Former is connected to a frozen LLM (e.g., OPT, FlanT5) in the vision-to-language generative learning stage, feeding the compact query representations into the LLM so BLIP-2 can perform zero-shot image-to-text generation following natural language instructions.

Claim: `claim_5b0567a72f03198708fcc77687c89bf0`

### flamingo-2204.14198v1

Requirement: `req_360e41c76c26117ed16af9d15221522b` · Status: `verified`

Flamingo bridges the frozen vision encoder and frozen LM via two learnable components: a Perceiver Resampler followed by freshly initialised cross-attention layers interleaved between the pretrained LM layers.
The Perceiver Resampler takes a variable number of image or video features from the vision encoder and produces a fixed, small number (64) of visual tokens via learned latent queries fed to a transformer stack that cross-attends to the flattened visual features, reducing the complexity of vision-text cross attention.
The visual tokens condition a frozen LM through freshly initialised cross-attention layers interleaved between pretrained LM layers, letting the LM incorporate visual information for next-token prediction while the language-only self-attention layers are kept frozen.

Claim: `claim_d4b3b4b1d5840530691f7119748f14b8`

Flamingo freezes the pretrained vision encoder (NFNet-F6) and keeps it frozen during the main training phase, freezes the pretrained LM weights so their initial capacity remains unchanged, and keeps the regular language-only self-attention layers frozen.
The trainable components are the newly added learnable architecture components: the Perceiver Resampler (with learnt latent queries) and the freshly initialised gated cross-attention layers interleaved between the frozen pretrained LM layers, which condition the LM on visual tokens.

During the main training phase, the vision encoder is left frozen and the pretrained LM weights are frozen (kept fully intact), including the regular language-only self-attention layers that are kept frozen during training.
In Stage 2, the trainable additions are the Perceiver Resampler and the freshly initialised gated cross-attention layers interleaved between the pretrained LM layers, which use visual tokens to condition the frozen LM.

## training objective · Verified findings

### blip-2-2301.12597v1

Requirement: `req_c2f9e90a793c063a0bd252bd1e597cb0` · Status: `verified`

BLIP-2 pre-trains its Q-Former in two stages: a first vision-language representation learning stage with a frozen image encoder, and a second vision-to-language generative learning stage with a frozen LLM.
In the representation learning stage, three pre-training objectives inspired by BLIP are jointly optimized with shared input format and model parameters, each using a different attention masking strategy between queries and text to control their interaction.
The representation learning stage trains the Q-Former so its queries learn to extract visual representation most informative of the text, while the generative stage connects the Q-Former to a frozen LLM and uses projected query embeddings as soft visual prompts to condition the LLM on the Q-Former's visual representation.
The first (representation learning) stage jointly optimizes three pre-training objectives inspired by BLIP, sharing the same input format and model parameters, with each objective using a different query-text attention masking strategy.
The first stage aims to train the Q-Former such that its queries learn to extract visual representation that is most informative of the text, using image-text pairs with a frozen image encoder.
The second (generative pre-training) stage connects the Q-Former with frozen image encoder to a frozen LLM, projecting query embeddings via a fully-connected layer to the LLM text embedding dimension and prepending them as soft visual prompts.
The second stage harvests the frozen LLM's generative language capability, with the Q-Former acting as an information bottleneck that feeds useful visual information and mitigates catastrophic forgetting.
